title: Opus 5.5 spent 43 million output tokens building 3D PvZ 2: Reflourished
author: Fun-Meaning-6474
selftext:
I really wanted to push this new opus by giving it something absolutely humungous, something that would test it across all aspects like long term and modular systems engineering, making 1000+ models with rigs and putting all of that together, that's why I chose PVZ

|Stat|Value|
|:-|:-|
|Output tokens|43,784,205|
|Equivalent API price for output tokens|$875.68|

it took far more than one prompt, and the session spanned over 30 hours across 2 days off work, sometimes using more than 100 sub-agents at a time, it also required a shit ton of research for the model to understand what I want and a lot of redirections from me inside blender regarding rigs, models and the UI inside the game itself, it was very much an involving process, not "hand off the wheel" type thing

the game runs entirely in the browser, with models and animations made in blender(the game is still a bit unfinished, but I do plan on polishing it up). If you guys encounter any bugs or issues feel free to leave a comment about it

Play the game here:  [https://pvz-2-reflourished-clone.vercel.app/](https://pvz-2-reflourished-clone.vercel.app/)  
Setup: claude 20x max subscription connected to blender with blendermcp inside [atomic.chat](http://atomic.chat)

comments.author: LucidFir
comments.body:
hey I'm not going to be able to do this until January, but I've got it in my head that I want to rebuild neverwinter nights in the baldurs gate 1 infinity engine. 

what do you reckon i need to know for this?

there's already an open source infinity engine project, and i believe similar projects for nwn

replies.author: Ball_Analytics
replies.body:
if you're dead set on the engine I'd start messing around with it now, to know the ins and outs of them, took me a day to or the waking parts of one when I was free, like 3/5 hours to figure out, assets, blender, and godot for a project I'm working on, then after another 6 hours to start the base of it. Once I got rid of the friction it was all smooth sailing. 

  
Two principles I haven't left behind is DRY (Do not repeat yourself) and TDD (Test Driven Development) otherwise, if you already know git, commit gates help a lot as well. (won't commit until your code is sound) CI/CD. git-lfs as well <- you'll be dealing with big files and that's if you're using git btw. (never had the opportunity of using it never had large files to commit)

  
By January you won't need to know much past this, because it's moved so fast this year, I reckon the prompt clone nwn will just create the whole game lol.

comments.author: AdFinancial4846
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/9uw2h8jf8rrh1.png?width=2527&format=png&auto=webp&s=f4f5018026bad9bf252e8025afaf77b02ba3565a

I played up to this level where the game then seemingly broke and I was unable to place any more plants. I will give my review up to that point.

The game have essentially no balance. You can do anything and win. With the multiple choices of plants I only used the rudimentary pea shooter and completed every level barely trying.

There's no introduction to new plants or mechanics that require them. Every enemy is a zombie or a zombie with more life, and they all die by being shot by peas or being run over by the insta kill lawnmowers.

The game is laggy. Not considering the zombies that only seem to move at a bearable frame rate by putting the game in 2x speed, every level takes a very long time to load, and there are large frame drops on completing each level.

Assuming there is a more balanced late game it would not be worth it going through the monotony, lag, and bugs to get there.
